Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • Acute upper-lip swelling, throat tightness, breathing difficulty, chest discomfort, dizziness within 30 min of eating prawn soup tonight; suspected anaphylaxis.  
  • Past similar episode ≈1 year ago after late-night curry (self-reported swelling and breathing difficulty).  
  • Known peanut allergy (history of childhood anaphylaxis requiring hospital care).  
  • Diagnosed asthma; uses salbutamol inhaler.  
  • New possible shellfish (prawn) allergy.

Management Plan

- Immediate actions:
  • Suspected anaphylaxis – clinician arranged emergency ambulance transport to hospital.  
  • Advised patient (and mother) to administer available antihistamine while awaiting ambulance.  
  • Instructed mother to stay with patient and inform emergency services of suspected anaphylaxis.

- Follow-up recommendations:
  • Post-hospital review with primary care to discuss long-term allergy management, including provision of epinephrine auto-injector, written anaphylaxis action plan, and prescription of regular non-sedating antihistamine if indicated.  
  • Asthma review and consideration of preventive (brown) inhaler.  
  • Education on allergen avoidance (peanut, possible shellfish) and medical alert identification.  
  • Schedule comprehensive Indigenous Health Assessment once acute event resolved (update immunizations, preventive screening, lifestyle assessment, CTG registration, etc.).

Consider:
  • Referral to allergist for formal testing (peanut, shellfish, other allergens).  
  • Referral to asthma educator / respiratory nurse.  
  • CTG registration for medication subsidy and care coordination.  
  • Dietitian input for safe nutritional planning if multiple food allergies confirmed.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note):

● Missing but clinically expected elements: BP, pulse, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, weight/BMI, waist circumference, mental health screening, alcohol and smoking history, immunization review, oral/eye/ear exams, urinalysis, preventive screening status.  
● Internal contradictions: None detected.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; limited routine health data captured due to emergency nature of consult.
